title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the 'équation des lacets' part of the Longue Marche notes, Grothendieck studies the outer Galois action on the profinite fundamental group(oid) of the modular curve, presumably M_{1,1} or the λ-line M_{0,4}. The base points are the two elliptic points: ρ (j=0, stabiliser of order 6) and σ (j=1728, λ=1/2, stabiliser of order 4). μ = {±1} is the central subgroup coming from -1 in SL_2.

First lines. These finish the proposition from the previous page. The canonical map M → 𝔖^*/Π_0 respects filtrations whose graded pieces are μ, 𝔖_3 and μ. The injective homomorphism obtained there is therefore an isomorphism, because 'les groupes en présence ont même ordre 24' (2·6·2 = 24).

Section d) Goal. Apply this to the structure of the 'double-base-point' group M_{ρ,σ} and define a homomorphism M → M_{ρ,σ}/μ_ρ.

(48) M_{ρ,σ} is defined as an iterated fibre product N^*_ρ ×_Γ N^*_σ ×_Γ G_{ρ,σ} over Γ_{ρ,σ}. Concretely it is a triple consisting of:
- an element of the normaliser of the inertia L_ρ at ρ;
- an element of the normaliser of L_σ at σ;
- an element of the global group G_{ρ,σ} ≅ M.
All three must have the same image in Γ_{ρ,σ}.

(49) records the ingredients:
- G_{ρ,σ} ≅ M = M(0)·𝔖^{+∧}, with M(0) ≅ M_{0,3}(0), i.e. a Galois-type group attached to the tripod.
- Γ_{ρ,σ} = G_{ρ,σ}/𝔖^{+∧} ≅ Π_Q^~, a Galois group of Q, which M(0) maps onto.
- N^*_ρ, N^*_σ are the normalisers in M of the local groups L_ρ, L_σ.

(50) recalls two subgroups introduced on pp. 615–616:
- Z^!_σ = M(1/2) ⊂ N^*_σ, the decomposition-type group at λ=1/2.
- N^?_ρ = Z^!_ρ·μ_ρ ⊂ N^*_ρ.

(51)–(52) state the key asymmetry:
- Z^!_σ meets μ trivially and maps isomorphically onto Γ_{ρ,σ} = Π_Q^~. So at σ the Galois group lifts with no sign ambiguity.
- N^?_ρ contains μ and is a central extension 1 → μ → N^?_ρ → Π_Q^~ → 1.

Next page. Using these, Grothendieck forms the subgroup M^⇆_{ρ,σ} = N^?_ρ ×_Γ Z^!_σ ×_Γ G. It is an extension of G ≅ M by μ_ρ, so dividing by μ_ρ gives the desired canonical map M → M_{ρ,σ}/μ_ρ.

Purpose. This builds a canonical Galois action on the pair of elliptic base points, or on paths between them, which is well defined up to the sign ±1 at ρ. This is the kind of bookkeeping needed to write the 'loop equation' (the GT-type relations coming from the elliptic points of order 2 and 3) as an equation in a well-defined group.
errors: (50), second line: the inclusion N^?_ρ ⊂ N^*_σ (as it appears in the transcription/image) is almost certainly a slip for N^*_ρ, since N^?_ρ is built from Z^!_ρ and μ at the base point ρ.

The 'cqfd' at the top depends on the previous page's proposition, which Grothendieck explicitly marks 'Admettant ce point' (compatibility of filtrations), so it is not fully proved there; and the inclusion N_ρ^* ∩ M_0^! ⊂ M'' carries a '?'. The order count (24 = 2·6·2) itself is consistent.
Notation is inconsistent between Γ_{ρ,σ} and γ_{ρ,σ} (same object). The underbrace label 𝔖_{ρ,σ} for 𝔖^{+∧} is not defined on the page.

ideas.what: Groupoid/two-base-point Galois group M_{ρ,σ} defined as a fibre product of the normalisers of the inertia at the two elliptic points with the global arithmetic fundamental group, over the Galois group of Q.
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on the profinite fundamental groupoid of M_{1,1} / M_{0,4} with (tangential) base points at the elliptic points; arithmetic fundamental groupoid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse) for the philosophy; worked out by Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps, Drinfeld (GT) in the 1990s
ideas.where_published: Philosophy only, in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), on the Teichmüller tower and the elliptic points of order 2 and 3 of M_{1,1}; this explicit construction appears unpublished

ideas.what: Asymmetry at the two elliptic points: the decomposition group at σ (λ=1/2) lifts Gal(Q̄/Q) isomorphically with no sign, while at ρ one only gets a central extension by μ=±1.
ideas.modern_name: Splitting / non-splitting of decomposition groups at elliptic points; sign ambiguity from -1 ∈ SL_2 (SL_2 vs PSL_2 lifts)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Nakamura's and Lochak–Schneps' treatments of GT acting on SL_2(Ẑ)-type groups

ideas.what: Filtration argument: M → 𝔖^*/Π_0 compatible with filtrations with graded pieces μ, 𝔖_3, μ; injective map between groups of order 24 is an isomorphism.
ideas.modern_name: Elementary group theory (comparison of finite quotients)

missed.claim: An explicit construction of a canonical Galois lift relative to the two elliptic base points ρ, σ, well defined only modulo the central μ_ρ. It serves to make the 'équation des lacets' (loop equation at the elliptic points) an equation in a well-defined group. The precise bookkeeping of which sign ambiguity can be removed (at σ yes, at ρ no) is a detail not usually stated in this form in the GT literature.
missed.quote: Le premier de ces groupes ne contient pas μ, le deuxième le contient ... Z_σ^! ⥲ Γ_{ρ,σ} = Π_Q^~ ; 1 → μ → N_ρ^? → Γ_{ρ,σ} → 1 exacte
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Relevant to precise formulations of GT actions on profinite SL_2(Z) / M_{1,1} with elliptic base points (Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps, Hoshi–Mochizuki style anabelian work). The sign (±1) bookkeeping is a known subtle point. Likely already implicit in the literature, so the novelty is modest.

deep.surprise_reason: A technical bookkeeping page inside Grothendieck's own (unpublished) development of the Galois action on the modular groupoid with elliptic base points. The mathematics is consistent with and largely subsumed by later GT theory; only the specific construction and its sign analysis are unpublished details.
transcription_corrections: First line should read roughly: 'en présence ont même ordre 24, et l'on en déduit un iso, cqfd.' It continues 'comme les groupes' from the previous page; '120' is a misreading of 'iso'.
(48): the fibre products are over γ_{ρ,σ} (lowercase gamma in the manuscript), the same as Γ_{ρ,σ} in (49).
(49): the underbrace under 𝔖^{+∧} is labelled 𝔖_{ρ,σ}; the parenthetical after Π_Q^~ is '(⇐ M(0))', i.e. M(0) surjects/maps onto it.
(50): the second line reads N^?_ρ = Z^!_ρ · μ_ρ (subscript likely ρ, not τ), with a crossed-out 'p' before Z.
(52): the second line is the exact sequence 1 → μ → N^?_ρ → γ_{ρ,σ} → 1, with marginal note 'γ_{ρ,σ} = Π_Q^~, exacte'.
